human.title: Ecuador: Chinese copper, American money, and a share that rose from nothing
human.author: AI-drafted from the site's indicators; not yet reviewed by the project owner
human.text_md:
## Alignment

Ecuador's index leans toward China, 35.2 against 15.7 in 2024 [index_value:influence:CN:2024] [index_value:influence:US:2024]. The trade is new and concentrated: of US$4.2 bn of mineral exports in 2025, 47% went to China and 12% to the United States; copper from the Mirador mine, US$1.7 bn, went US$1.6 bn to China, while gold, US$2.4 bn, went more to the United States (US$514 m) than to China (US$308 m) [concentration:share_cn_x:2025] [flow_trade:ECU:copper:2025] [flow_trade:ECU:gold:2025]. The money runs the other way in the latest years: Chinese commitments were US$4.5 bn over 2015–2021 (with US$4.5 bn in 2014 alone, before the window), the DFC committed US$683 m in 2015–2021 and US$1.5 bn in 2022–2024, the largest recent US commitments to any of the twelve [flow_finance:CN:ECU:2015-2021] [flow_finance:US:ECU:2022-2024]. The six executive statements score 0.00 toward China over four coded positions and give no coded position on the United States; the five statements by US officials carry no negative on China [statement:stance_cn:ECU:2025-2026] [statement:count:bloc=United States:ECU]. My reading: Ecuador is where the two powers' instruments are most clearly split, Chinese offtake and American credit, and the words do not take sides.

## Trajectory

The Chinese share of exports was 0.0% in 2008, 2.6% in 2012, 9.5% in 2016, 33% in 2020 and 47% in 2025, the steepest climb in the region, following the Mirador copper mine [concentration:share_cn_x:2016] [concentration:share_cn_x:2025]. Seven large commitments are flagged, the oil-backed loans of 2011–2014, and one of them was followed by no change in where the minerals went [anomaly_flag:large_commitment] [anomaly_flag:finance_without_trade_response]. The window after the 2017 US critical-minerals order shows the share to China rising 22 points, which is the mine opening, not the order [event_effect:us_eo13817_critical_minerals:CN:window:ECU]. No legislative records or headlines are coded [coverage:ECU].

## Risks and likely next moves

The models put China's share at 61% in 2030 at baseline, 71% under the China pull and 51% under US reshoring, the highest floor in the region; the US share reaches 19% under reshoring [forecast:export_share:CN:us_reshoring:2030:ECU] [forecast:export_share:US:us_reshoring:2030:ECU]. Parity would take US$718 m of yearly exports switching, 1.4 times current US purchases, and copper alone could cover it [insights:parity_gap:ECU]. My reading: the DFC's 2022–2024 commitments are the test case for whether American credit changes where ore is sold; the copper row for 2026 and 2027 will answer it.

## What would change this reading

A copper export row to a destination other than China; a second copper mine with a non-Chinese offtaker; or a DFC commitment tied to a mineral rather than to other sectors.
